method: Hand-written single-best-answer MCQs grounded only in the accepted open full text.

topic.topicDisplayName: Septic arthritis: diagnosis, Gram stain, joint aspiration, empirical antibiotics, surgical drainage
topic.coverageNote: Same SANJO guideline, with questions on aspiration timing, Gram stain, and drainage.

mcqs.question: If only a little synovial fluid is obtained, what is the analysis priority?

options.A: Bacterial identification, then white-cell count including PMN percentage, then crystals
options.E: The guideline says not to prioritize

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Bacterial identification, then white-cell count including PMN percentage, then crystals
mcqs.explanation: Priority if volume is limited is bacterial identification, white-cell count with PMN percentage, then crystals.

sourceRefs.excerpt: white blood cell count including polymorphonuclear (PMN) percentage, and presence of crystals (in that priority order if the quantity of liquid is not enough

mcqs.question: How should a synovial white-cell count above 50,000 per microlitre be used?

options.A: It suggests septic arthritis but is not sufficient alone
options.B: It confirms septic arthritis without culture
options.E: The guideline does not use a 50,000 threshold

mcqs.correctAnswerText: It suggests septic arthritis but is not sufficient alone
mcqs.explanation: A count above 50,000/µL suggests septic arthritis but alone is not sufficient for the diagnosis.

sourceRefs.excerpt: A synovial white blood cell count of > 50 000 cells µ L - 1 is suggestive of SANJO, but alone is not sufficient for the diagnosis

mcqs.question: What does a synovial white-cell count below 25,000 per microlitre mean?

options.A: It decreases the post-test probability but does not exclude septic arthritis
options.E: It is the threshold for antibiotics before culture

mcqs.correctAnswerText: It decreases the post-test probability but does not exclude septic arthritis
mcqs.explanation: A count below 25,000/µL lowers post-test probability but cannot exclude septic arthritis. Cut-offs may not apply in immunosuppressed patients.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Low synovial white blood cell count ( < 25 000 cells µ L - 1 ) decreases post-test probability, but it cannot exclude SANJO

mcqs.question: Why perform a Gram stain despite limited sensitivity?

options.A: Specificity is excellent, so a positive stain is early proof of infection and can guide empirical treatment
options.C: A negative stain ends the work-up
options.E: The guideline advises against Gram stain

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Specificity is excellent, so a positive stain is early proof of infection and can guide empirical treatment
mcqs.explanation: Gram stain is recommended despite limited sensitivity because excellent specificity can provide early proof of infection and help guide empirical treatment.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Performing Gram staining on synovial fluid is recommended despite its limited sensitivity; given its excellent specificity, it can provide early proof of infection and help guiding empirical treatment

mcqs.question: How should the remaining fluid be cultured?

options.A: Inoculate blood-culture bottles; also plate sterile-tube fluid on agar and enrichment broth; incubate 5–7 days
options.B: A dry swab of the skin is sufficient
options.C: Culture is optional if the white-cell count is high

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Inoculate blood-culture bottles; also plate sterile-tube fluid on agar and enrichment broth; incubate 5–7 days
mcqs.explanation: Remaining fluid should go into blood-culture bottles. Sterile-tube fluid should be plated on agar and thioglycolate enrichment broth as well or instead. Incubation of 5–7 days is recommended according to local practice.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Synovial fluid from a sterile tube should be plated on agar plates and enrichment broth (thioglycolate)
